subject: Startups
title: Timing and Market Windows
description: A short lesson to help you apply Timing and Market Windows.

hook.text: Bill Gross studied 200 startups and found the number-one factor in success wasn't the team or idea. It was timing.

buildup.text: Uber launched when smartphones had GPS and mapping. Five years earlier, the tech wasn't ready.

discovery.text: Market windows open when technology matures, costs drop, or behavior shifts. Unicorns ride these windows perfectly.

twist.text: Webvan tried grocery delivery in 2000 and failed. Instacart did it in 2012 and became a unicorn.

climax.text: Zoom existed for years before COVID. The pandemic opened a market window that catapulted it from niche to essential.

punchline.text: The right idea at the wrong time is the wrong idea.

quiz.question: What did Bill Gross's study find was the top factor in startup success?
